item.title: Literally the hardest thing I've done, but I'm out.
item.description:
For those that might remember, this is me: https://imgur.com/gallery/bQyanwL Last night, after using the time my partner was away on a trip to pack and prep, I left a note and my keys and closed the door on 15 years together. I knew it would be hard, but I didnt expect the gut wrenching sobs that escaped my mouth when I started down the driveway. I didnt think I'd spend the last 4 days second guessing my choice and wondering if the problem was really just that I hadn't tried hard enough. But I also didn't expect them to chase me through the house, throwing punches, kicks, bottles and insults before they left.
So I packed my shit. Literally all of it. what you see there is the sum total of my life hastily packed away and stuffed in my only other sole possession. Made plans to drive out to family 2500 miles away who I haven't seen in over a decade. But I had to rush at the end. My partner forced the truth out of me and, to my surprise, broke down in tears rather than anger. They said they wouldnt try to stop me but begged me to at least let them say goodbye so we didn't end on them assaulting me. So much of me believed them and felt terrible for making them cry. I wanted to stay so badly to say goodbye. But I didnt, because I knew it wouldn't be that simple, and I couldn't be that strong. I left before they got home, blocked their number, and drove through the middle of the night.
My biggest regret is leaving this girl behind. Leaving early meant not having the time I wanted to say goodbye. She knew something was up all weekend and anxiously stayed by me. In the end all I could give her for a goodbye was a bully stick and a hug. She was always "my" dog. I was her favorite since she was a puppy and would line her stuffed toys up along the window and wait for me to come home.
But I'm moving. This morning's sunrise from the road felt good. I'm anxious about money being tight since I had to leave so suddenly, but I cant stop now. I'm still bursting into tears, I'm still mourning not being able to have my pup with me, and this is still the hardest fucking thing I've ever done, but I'm doing it. See you on the road. Edit: Thanks for all the support everyone!!! I absolutely couldn't have taken this step without the support and experiences shared by others here. If you're thinking of getting out, I hope this can inspire you and stoke the courage that I know is already inside you. Since a few folks have asked, I opened a Ko-Fi for those that want to help me get to where I'm going and get my footing once I'm there. https://ko-fi.com/kechirtravels

item.title: Mia Heller water filter
item.description: https://www.reddit.com/r/MemesForGirls/s/uPOwqCkSbo https://www.smithsonianmag.com/innovation/this-high-school-student-invented-a-filter-that-eliminates-96-percent-of-microplastics-from-drinking-water-180988363/ https://thewaternetwork.com/article-FfV/high-school-student-invented-a-filter-that-eliminates-96-percent-of-microplastics-TsPj-KNnaEefuH6kPyUBiQ Quick fact: What's the difference between primary and secondary microplastics? According to the EPA, primary microplastics are tiny plastics manufactured for things like cosmetics and biomedical products. Secondary microplastics are plastic pieces that have broken down from larger plastic consumer products. A new take on water filtration While several water filtration systems are available, they aren’t all efficient and easily accessible to everyone. Traditional systems often rely primarily on chemical treatments and may also require labor-intensive upkeep and frequent membrane changes. They also come with high price tags and maintenance costs. In the spring of 2024, Heller had the idea for her filtration system, but she really got working on it in the summer of 2025. By early January of that year, after tinkering in her garage and kitchen, she had a working prototype. “It was essentially just a container,” she says. Within the container was her filtration system, what she called a “spinning magnified vial.” Heller harnessed a reusable magnetic oil called ferrofluid to selectively bind to microplastic particles as water flows through her filtration system. While her model successfully filtered out the microplastics from the water in two simple steps, the system still required constant maintenance, as it did not self-recycle the ferrofluid. “But if I could create a system that was able to basically clean itself and reuse material," she explains, “the maintenance needs could go down by a lot.” Determined to find an answer, Heller continued experimenting. One of the main obstacles she faced was figuring out how to place her units so that the ferrofluid—a liquid thicker than water—would be able to move into the water chamber above it without getting clogged. Along with the ferrofluid flow, the process of magnetic separation followed by the recovery of ferrofluid also needed to work together as one system rather than competing with each other.

item.title: Nepo baby says what?
item.description: Governor Sanders, the facts tell a very different story. According to USDA data, 39% of SNAP recipients are CHILDREN and another 20% are SENIORS. In FY2023, 88% of recipients lived in households containing a child, senior, or person with a disability. And Arkansas has already tried Medicaid work requirements. By 2019, approximately 18,000 Arkansans had lost healthcare coverage, while researchers found NO significant increase in employment. More than 95% of the targeted population already met the requirements or qualified for exemptions. Those are the facts. The overwhelming majority aren’t simply people choosing not to work. They’re children, seniors, people with disabilities, working families, and people struggling financially. The question isn’t whether able-bodied adults should work. It’s whether additional requirements actually increase employment or instead create bureaucratic barriers that take assistance away from eligible people. Arkansas already ran that experiment. The documented results deserve more attention than political advertising.

Thank you for showcasing interest in it :) patreon/mcroft07 The paint isn’t edible (gross) I've been painting myself for 16 years. The 07 does not mean I was born in 2007, UK 7 is my shoe size No, I don't need help painting my back, I don't want to paint my back, I don't need to paint my back. (also gross) No, I don't need help washing it off. (also you are gross) If you want to see more I am MCroft07 on IG, twitter, Tiktok, YouTube I paint them live on twitch I like doing the lip syncs, they're fun for me while I paint them. I couldn’t care less if you think they’re cringe. I am cringe but I am free My tattoos on my ribs are from Tomb Raider - I am a big TR fan I do not have an OF but if you want to send me money THAT badly you can just tip my twitch account. Haha. The shower afterwards takes about 15 minutes, I use a regular sponge and shower gel. The reason why it can look different at the end is because I am wearing a wig, I promise you it is not a different person because the hair changed. While on this topic, if my eyes change colour it’s because I am wearing contact lenses. (Those with an IQ above 10… I know. Even I’m shocked the wig thing is a frequent comment). I use body paint. It doesn’t tickle, I am very ticklish and this is fine. I don’t have an allergic reaction to the paint, but if you do it, you should always do a patch test first I do not know where you can buy body paint in every country. I know in the UK it is available at FacePaintingshop.com. I use a plethora of different brands, it’s best to search for them yourself online. I don’t work in Hollywood, I don’t want to. I just want to improve my body painting for myself. I am English, not American. I do not go outside like this to scare people. 1, that would be very cold. 2, in this current age, everyone would take photos without me knowing and it would likely dox me :)))))) I’m not a sweaty person, but if I was this would be a lot more difficult. Thank you to those of you who came from Imgur to my Twitch channel! “What’s the point in painting yourself when you can wear clothes?” all my clothes are in the laundry, had to resort to this, tough life It would not be quicker to jump into a pool of paint - think of the drying time?! If I did a Spyro makeup look on wednesday and it has gotten me in the mood to play Spyro again but I have heard so much about Dispatch so I think I'm going to play that on twitch tonight :) I'm super excited! I hope I find new characters to paint in it but my friend told me that there is a man's ding dong in the first ten minutes I don’t care that I wash it off at the end, I get to reuse this canvas, we love a reduce, reuse, recycle queen. I am not the lady who did the Maneskin video, it’s a cool video and she slayed, but it isn’t me. I can promise you there is not *a man* painting these and I am pretending to paint myself. I am genuinely painting myself. I know a lot of you don’t like reading this faq because it is horrid to see that I have to answer all of these. Unfortunately I have noticed that when I don’t put in all the icky things then I get more gross comments and I just have to spend more time blocking people so it’s better to call it out. I just copy and paste it each time anyway.

item.description: BRENDAN FRASER IS GETTING READY TO RETURN AS RICK O’CONNELL! Brendan Fraser is reportedly getting back into shape ahead of his return as Rick O’Connell in The Mummy 4. At 57, Fraser is reportedly putting in the work to bring back the charisma, humor and physicality that made Rick one of the most iconic adventure heroes of the late ’90s and early 2000s. The original Mummy movies turned Fraser into a major action star, and seeing him back as Rick after all these years feels like the kind of comeback fans have been waiting for. Plot details are still being kept under wraps, but if Fraser really is preparing to step back into the role, Rick O’Connell might be coming back exactly where he belongs: in the middle of the action.
